nodes.label: Add nav link

nodes.label: Monitor list screen
nodes.detail: Renders $root.monitorList as is. It never fetches anything itself

nodes.label: List row link
nodes.detail: Each row of the list. A router-link that opens the details screen on click

nodes.label: Bulk pause menu
nodes.detail: The "Pause" item in the action menu while in selection mode

nodes.label: Bulk resume menu
nodes.detail: The "Resume" item in the action menu while in selection mode

nodes.label: Bulk delete menu
nodes.detail: The "Delete" item in the action menu while in selection mode

nodes.label: Bulk pause confirm
nodes.detail: Confirm dialog for a bulk pause. Yes continues to pause

nodes.label: Bulk delete confirm
nodes.detail: Confirm dialog for a bulk delete. Yes continues to delete

nodes.label: Monitor details screen
nodes.detail: Screen that shows one monitor's details and its action buttons

nodes.label: Pause button
nodes.detail: Pause button on the details screen (shown only while monitor.active is true)

nodes.label: Resume button
nodes.detail: Resume button on the details screen. Disabled while forceInactive

nodes.label: Edit link
nodes.detail: Link from the details screen to /edit/:id

nodes.label: Delete button
nodes.detail: Delete button on the details screen

nodes.label: Pause confirm
nodes.detail: Confirm dialog for pause. Yes continues to pause

nodes.label: Delete confirm
nodes.detail: Confirm dialog for delete. For a group it also offers to delete the children

nodes.label: Form init
nodes.detail: On add it fills in the defaults; on edit or clone it fetches the existing values with getMonitor

nodes.label: Save handler
nodes.detail: After validation, add sends "add" and edit sends "editMonitor"

nodes.label: add emit
nodes.detail: socket.emit("add", monitor, callback). A pure pass-through

nodes.label: Refetch the list
nodes.detail: socket.emit("getMonitorList", callback). Used for an explicit refetch from another screen

nodes.label: Delete emit
nodes.detail: socket.emit("deleteMonitor", id, deleteChildren, callback)

nodes.label: List received
nodes.detail: socket.on("monitorList") replaces this.monitorList wholesale

nodes.label: Update diff received
nodes.detail: socket.on("updateMonitorIntoList") swaps only the matching ID

nodes.label: Delete diff received
nodes.detail: socket.on("deleteMonitorFromList") removes it from this.monitorList

nodes.label: Heartbeat received
nodes.detail: socket.on("heartbeat") appends to heartbeatList and updates the graphs

nodes.label: Pause emit
nodes.detail: Calls getSocket().emit("pauseMonitor", monitor.id, cb) directly

nodes.label: Resume emit
nodes.detail: Calls getSocket().emit("resumeMonitor", monitor.id, cb) directly

nodes.label: Delete emit
nodes.detail: Calls $root.deleteMonitor(monitor.id, deleteChildrenMonitors, cb)

nodes.label: Displayed data reference
nodes.detail: Just reads the entry out of $root.monitorList by $route.params.id (no new fetch)

nodes.label: Bulk pause emit
nodes.detail: Sends pauseMonitor one by one to the selected running monitors

nodes.label: Bulk resume emit
nodes.detail: Sends resumeMonitor one by one to the selected paused monitors

nodes.label: Bulk delete emit
nodes.detail: Sends deleteMonitor(id,false,cb) one by one to the selected monitors

nodes.label: Socket connection
nodes.detail: The client connection is established. Every socket.on handler below is registered inside this scope

nodes.label: add received
nodes.detail: Handler for adding a new monitor

nodes.label: editMonitor received
nodes.detail: Handler for saving an edit to an existing monitor

nodes.label: getMonitorList received
nodes.detail: Handler for an explicit request to refetch the list

nodes.label: getMonitor received
nodes.detail: Fetches one monitor (used to fill the edit/clone form)

nodes.label: resumeMonitor received
nodes.detail: Handler for starting or resuming a monitor

nodes.label: pauseMonitor received
nodes.detail: Handler for pausing a monitor

nodes.label: deleteMonitor received
nodes.detail: Handler for deleting a monitor. For a group, the fate of the children can be chosen

nodes.label: Check login
nodes.detail: Throws if socket.userID is not set

nodes.label: Push the lists after login
nodes.detail: Entry function that pushes the lists, notifications and more in one go after a successful login

nodes.label: Check owner
nodes.detail: Checks that the given monitorID exists under that user_id. Throws if it does not

nodes.label: Update notification links
nodes.detail: Deletes every monitor_notification row, then recreates only the selected ones

nodes.label: Start / resume
nodes.detail: Sets active=1 and, if an instance already exists, stops it before starting again

nodes.label: Restart
nodes.detail: A thin wrapper that just calls startMonitor again

nodes.label: Pause
nodes.detail: Sets active=0 and stops the running instance if there is one

nodes.label: Send the list
nodes.detail: Broadcasts the result of getMonitorJSONList on the monitorList event

nodes.label: Send the update diff
nodes.detail: Rebuilds only the given ID and broadcasts it on updateMonitorIntoList

nodes.label: Send the delete notice
nodes.detail: Broadcasts just the ID on the deleteMonitorFromList event

nodes.label: Build the list JSON
nodes.detail: Reads the user_id's monitors from the DB and returns objects shaped by toJSON

nodes.label: To JSON
nodes.detail: Turns one DB row into the object the screen renders

nodes.label: Prepare preload data
nodes.detail: Preloads notifications, tags, child IDs, active state and more in one pass (avoids N+1)

nodes.label: Active check
nodes.detail: Combines its own active flag with the parent's state to decide whether it really runs

nodes.label: List child IDs
nodes.detail: Recursively collects the IDs of every descendant monitor

nodes.label: Get children
nodes.detail: Fetches the rows whose parent is the given ID

nodes.label: Unlink the children
nodes.detail: Sets the children's parent to null (ungroups them)

nodes.label: Delete one
nodes.detail: Stops the instance if it is running, then deletes the row from the monitor table

nodes.label: Recursive delete
nodes.detail: For a group, recursively deletes the children first and then itself

nodes.label: Start monitoring
nodes.detail: Starts the heartbeat loop (beat)

nodes.label: Stop monitoring
nodes.detail: Clears the setTimeout and sets isStop=true to end the loop

nodes.label: Run a heartbeat
nodes.detail: The resident loop that checks the target, saves the heartbeat and re-schedules the next run with setTimeout

nodes.label: monitor table
nodes.detail: The monitor itself: id / active / parent / user_id and more. user_id is ON DELETE SET NULL

nodes.label: heartbeat table
nodes.detail: One check result per monitor_id. ON DELETE CASCADE when the monitor is deleted

nodes.label: monitor_notification table
nodes.detail: The join table of monitor_id x notification_id. ON DELETE CASCADE when the monitor is deleted

flows.title: Add a monitor
flows.trigger: Clicking the "Add" link in the sidebar

steps.label: isAdd, so defaults are filled into the form (no server call)
Fill in the required fields and click Save
Throws before saving unless every accepted_statuscodes entry is a string
DELETE, then INSERT only the selected ones
Prepare the preload data (see the list flow for details)
If monitor.active !== false, start right away
Start the beat loop through safeBeat()
Re-schedule the next run with setTimeout

notes: If accepted_statuscodes is not an array of strings it throws before saving, and nothing is written to the DB
Unless active is explicitly false at creation time, startMonitor is called as part of the save and monitoring begins immediately

flows.title: Edit a monitor
flows.trigger: Clicking the "Edit" link on the details screen

steps.label: For isEdit/isClone it emits getMonitor directly (never through app.socket.*)
Fetch one row by id + user_id
With no matching row, monitor is undefined and reading monitor.id raises a TypeError
Fill the fetched values into the form
isEdit, so editMonitor is emitted directly (app.socket.editMonitor does not exist)
Fetch the row by id alone (not narrowed by user_id)
With no matching row, reading bean.user_id raises a TypeError
Parent cycle check (is monitor.parent one of its own descendants?)
Naming a descendant as the parent gives 'Invalid Monitor Group'
Unlinks the children only when the type changed from group to something else
UPDATE the children's parent to null
DELETE, then INSERT only the selected ones
Decide whether it should run after the save
If an instance already exists, stop it first
init() runs again whether it succeeded or failed, refetching with getMonitor

notes: If the target monitor does not exist, reading bean.user_id raises a TypeError that is caught. The user never sees an explicit message such as 'Permission denied.'
After saving, init() is called again whether or not res.ok is true, and the form is refetched with getMonitor (lines 4386-4395)
editMonitor does not go through the mixins/socket.js wrapper (app.socket.*); EditMonitor.vue's submit() calls getSocket().emit() directly

flows.title: Pause a monitor
flows.trigger: Clicking the "Pause" button on the details screen

steps.label: getSocket().emit("pauseMonitor", id, cb) (app.socket.* is not involved)
Missing or not owned gives 'You do not own this monitor.'
clearTimeout cancels the next beat (the monitoring loop stops)
active turns false and the button switches to Resume
Select several in the list and pause them at once
Emit pauseMonitor individually for each selected running monitor
The same pauseMonitor handler runs once per monitor

notes: checkOwner does not distinguish a monitor that does not exist from one owned by someone else: both get the same 'You do not own this monitor.'
The details screen's pauseMonitor skips the mixins/socket.js wrapper and calls getSocket().emit() directly

flows.title: Resume a monitor
flows.trigger: Clicking the "Resume" button on the details screen

steps.label: Runs resumeMonitor() immediately, with no confirm dialog
It really is startMonitor (shared by start, resume and restart)
Missing or not owned gives 'You do not own this monitor.'
If an instance is still around, stop it first (prevents a double start)
active turns true and the button switches to Pause
Runs resumeSelected() immediately, with no confirm dialog
Emit resumeMonitor individually for each selected paused monitor
The same resumeMonitor handler runs once per monitor

notes: resumeMonitor is really startMonitor: the auto-start on add, the restart after an edit and the resume from a pause all go through the same svc.server.startMonitor
A child under a paused parent group becomes forceInactive, which disables the Resume button on the details screen (Details.vue:127)
Unlike pause, the bulk resume in the list has no confirm dialog (MonitorList.vue:73)

flows.title: Delete a monitor
flows.trigger: Clicking the "Delete" button on the details screen

steps.label: Click Yes (for a group, the delete-children checkbox is sent along)
Fetch the target by id + user_id (a miss is not an error)
Fetch the children only when type==='group'
If deleteChildren=true, recurse into each child
Recurse again if there are grandchildren
If an instance is running, stop it first
Broadcast deleteMonitorFromList for each deleted child
If deleteChildren=false, the children's parent is set to null (the default)
UPDATE the children's parent to null
Broadcast an update for each child that lost its parent
DELETE FROM monitor (heartbeat rows follow via CASCADE)
ON DELETE CASCADE removes the related heartbeat rows too
ON DELETE CASCADE removes the notification links too
The target itself is announced with deleteMonitorFromList as well
Remove it from the list too
callback({ok:true,'successDeleted'}) (the same success even when nothing matched)
Select several in the list and delete them at once
Send deleteMonitor(id,false,cb) once per selected monitor
The same deleteMonitor handler runs once per monitor

notes: The deleteMonitor handler does not throw when no row matches; it still returns callback({ok:true,'successDeleted'}) (server.js:1140/1179). A quiet success that deleted nothing is possible
heartbeat and monitor_notification rows go away through the DB's ON DELETE CASCADE. There is no explicit delete in the application code
When a group is deleted, deleteChildren=true recursively deletes the children, while false sets their parent to null and keeps them (the bulk delete in the list is always false)

flows.title: View the monitor list
flows.trigger: Logging in, or opening the monitor list screen

steps.label: Push the list right after login
Get the list JSON for this user_id
Fetch every row for the user_id, ordered by weight DESC then name
Fetch all notification links in one query
Collect the descendant IDs for each monitor in one pass
Fetch by parent = the given ID
For each monitor, combine its own state with its parent's
Another screen (EditMaintenance.vue and friends) emits getMonitorList explicitly

notes: MonitorList.vue and Dashboard.vue never call getMonitorList themselves. They keep using the data pushed by afterLogin -> sendMonitorList right after login as $root.monitorList

getMonitorList (app.socket.getMonitorList / api.socket.getMonitorList) is called to re-sync after edits on other screens such as EditMaintenance.vue and Tags.vue (never from the monitor list screen itself)

flows.title: Open the details screen
flows.trigger: Clicking a monitor row in the list

steps.label: The computed monitor looks it up by the route ID
Renders the $root.monitorList fetched at login, as is (no new fetch)
An ID missing from $root.monitorList yields undefined, which the template can error on
Push the check result in realtime (io.to(user_id).emit('heartbeat'))
It is appended to heartbeatList and the current state and graph update

notes: The details screen calls neither getMonitor nor getMonitorBeats; it only reads the $root.monitorList / $root.heartbeatList fetched at login (there is no per-monitor realtime subscription, Details.vue:503-507)

The getMonitorBeats handler at server.js:1053 and the wrapper method at mixins/socket.js:719 are both implemented, but searching the whole repository turns up no caller anywhere in the current front end (dead code). The actual line chart (PingChart.vue) uses $root.heartbeatList, which accumulates from the heartbeat event
